Producing a standalone executable (`--emit-exe`) drives a `clang`-compatible C
compiler at the final link to build the runtime. Point the compiler at it once:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('AEGIS_CC','C:\LLVM\bin\clang.exe','User')
```

```sh
export AEGIS_CC=/usr/bin/clang
```

Formatting and the other non-linking outputs need no C compiler. The Aegis
runtime is bundled with the toolchain, so you never build it.

## Run your first program

```sh
cat > hello.aegis <<'EOF'
struct Greeter { }
impl Greeter {
    fn greet(self) {
        println("hello, aegis")
    }
}
EOF

compiler hello.aegis --main Greeter::greet --emit-exe hello
./hello
# -> hello, aegis
```

`--emit-exe` produces a standalone executable (`.exe` suffix is appended on
Windows). Without an explicit filename the executable is written next to the
first input file under that file's basename; pass a path (`--emit-exe app.exe`)
to control it. `--emit-obj` emits an object file and `--fmt` prints the
canonical formatted source.

The entry point defaults to the method named `main` (an `impl X { fn main(self) }`)
and can be overridden with `--main X::y`. `main` may return `Int` (the exit
code), nothing (exit 0), or `Result[Empty, E]`: `return ok` exits 0, and
`return err(n)` exits with `n` when the error payload is an `Int` (any other
payload exits 1), giving CLIs an explicit non-zero exit-code path with `?`
propagation. There is no `args: List[String]` parameter — programs read
`argc()` and `arg(i)`, where `arg(0)` is the program path and real arguments
start at `arg(1)` (see [wordfreq CLI](examples.md) for a full argv-driven
program).

## Driving the compiler from an agent (MCP)

`aegis-mcp` exposes the same streaming pipeline as MCP tools and resources, so
an agent host (opencode and other MCP clients) can compile without a shell:
open a session, stream the source item by item, then link and run. Register it
with one command from your project root:

```sh
aegis init --tool opencode    # also: claude, cursor, vscode, windsurf, codex, all
```

Then restart the host. See [the `aegis` CLI](tooling.md) for the flags, the
per-host config files, and the
`create_session` → `stream_source` → `eos` → `link_object` → `run_object` loop.

## Standard library

The "stdlib" has two layers:

1. **Compiler builtins** - methods the compiler provides directly
   (`String.length`, `String.split/join/trim`, `String.to_upper/to_lower/
   repeat`, `List.map/filter/fold/sort/append/pop/length/contains/index_of/
   reverse`, `Map.length/contains/insert`,
   `Float.floor/sqrt`). See [stdlib](stdlib/index.md).
2. **Aegis seed modules** - ordinary `struct`/`impl` code in `stdlib/`
   (`mathstr.aegis`: `Int.min/max/abs`, `starts_with/ends_with/contains`,
   `String.to_int`; `stack.aegis`: `Stack.push/pop/peek/len`).

Seed modules are **not auto-loaded**: to use their methods, list the module
files among the compiler inputs, e.g.
`compiler stdlib/mathstr.aegis app.aegis --emit-exe app.exe`. Compiler
builtins (layer 1) need no file — they are always in scope.


# tooling

# Tooling: the `aegis` CLI

Every release ships a single front-end, `aegis`, next to the compiler and the
services. It is the recommended entry point:

```
aegis init        register the MCP server with your agent host
aegis mcp         run the MCP stdio server
aegis daemon      run the streaming WebSocket server
aegis ws          run the WebSocket client
aegis version     print the version
aegis <args...>   forward to the compiler
```

The last form forwards everything after `aegis` to the compiler, so
`aegis hello.aegis --main Greeter::greet --emit-exe hello` is exactly
`compiler hello.aegis --main Greeter::greet --emit-exe hello`.

## Registering an agent: `aegis init`

`aegis init` writes the `aegis-mcp` server into the config file of an agent host,
merging into any existing file so other servers are preserved:

```
aegis init --tool opencode     # also: claude, cursor, vscode, windsurf, codex, all
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--tool <name>` | Which host to configure (`opencode`, `claude`, `cursor`, `vscode`, `windsurf`, `codex`, or `all`) |
| `--global` | Write the user-level config instead of the project one |
| `--cc <path>` | Set `AEGIS_CC` (the C compiler used for the final link step) |
| `--force` | Accepted for symmetry; the `aegis` entry is always refreshed |

With no `--tool`, `init` detects the host from the current directory (an existing
`opencode.json`, `.cursor/`, `.vscode/`, `.mcp.json`, `mcp_config.json`, or
`.codex/`) and defaults to opencode when nothing is found. The registered
command is the absolute path to `aegis-mcp`, so the server needs no arguments.

| Host | Config file (project) | `--global` location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| opencode | `opencode.json` | `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` |
| Claude Code | `.mcp.json` | `~/.claude.json` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/mcp.json` | `~/.cursor/mcp.json` |
| VS Code | `.vscode/mcp.json` | (project only) |
| Windsurf | `mcp_config.json` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json` |
| Codex | `.codex/config.toml` | `~/.codex/config.toml` |

Restart the host after `init` so it picks up the server.

One environment variable matters to the server:

- `AEGIS_CC` names a `clang`-compatible C compiler. It is needed only to produce
  a standalone executable (`--emit-exe`) or to link and run an object over MCP
  (for example `C:\LLVM\bin\clang.exe` on Windows or `/usr/bin/clang` on Linux).
  `aegis init` records it in the server's environment; when it is unset, the
  tools that build executables report a clear error. Streaming, object emission,
  and formatting need no C compiler at all.

## What the agent gets

Once registered, the host sees the Aegis streaming pipeline as MCP tools and
the language corpus as MCP resources. The canonical loop is:

```
create_session  ->  stream_source  ->  eos  ->  link_object  ->  run_object
```

`create_session` opens an isolated compile session (optionally `--target` and a
workspace for C-WAL reopen); `stream_source` pushes source item by item with live
unresolved warnings; `eos` runs the end-of-stream gate and the full semantic
pass; `link_object` produces an executable; `run_object` executes it. The corpus
is served as `aegis://docs/<page>` and `aegis://stdlib/<module>`, plus
`aegis://llms.txt` and `aegis://llms-full.txt` for a one-shot bootstrap.

## Manual registration

`aegis init` is a convenience; the config is plain JSON (or TOML for Codex). For
opencode, for example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "aegis": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["C:/Aegis/bin/aegis-mcp.exe"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": { "AEGIS_CC": "C:/LLVM/bin/clang.exe" }
    }
  }
}
```

For Claude Code or Cursor, the same server goes under `mcpServers` with
`command`, `args`, and `env`. On Windows, `register-opencode.ps1` (shipped in the
archive) remains available for opencode-only setups.


# examples

# Real project: wordfreq CLI

The **wordfreq** project is a complete, two-module console application. It
exercises the same surface a normal CLI needs: cross-module visibility, a
`Map[String, Int]` accumulator, `List` iteration, `argc()`/`arg(i)` argv
parsing, and output formatting by string concatenation (`str(v)` + `+`).

## Layout

| File         | Role                                                                    |
|--------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `lib.aegis`  | `@module wordfreq`; `pub struct Frequencies` + `add` + `order_by_count` |
| `main.aegis` | `@module wordfreq_main`; `import @wordfreq`; `App::main` entry (default) |

## Build

One compiler command for the whole project, no hand-written C:

```text
aegis main.aegis lib.aegis --emit-exe wordfreq.exe
```

The entry point is `App::main`, found automatically as the default entry.
Running it:

```text
> wordfreq.exe the quick brown fox the lazy dog the
the: 3
brown: 1
dog: 1
fox: 1
lazy: 1
quick: 1
----
tokens=8 unique=6
```

## Notes on working around today's limits

The v1 closure rule (scalar captures only) means a `sort` comparator cannot
read the counts map, and index assignment targets are not yet supported, so
`order_by_count` is an explicit selection-sort over first-seen words
(`taken: Map[String, Bool]` guards extraction). The app reads via
`self.counts[w]` and appends into fresh lists — no index writes required.

# Flagship: the dungeon adventure

`examples/dungeon.aegis` is a stress test for the standard library: a
deterministic, argv-driven text adventure. Compiled alongside the seed modules
(`stdlib/mathstr.aegis`, `stdlib/stack.aegis`, `stdlib/set.aegis`), it runs a
fixed command script:

```text
aegis stdlib/mathstr.aegis stdlib/stack.aegis stdlib/set.aegis \
      examples/dungeon.aegis --main Dungeon::run --emit-exe dungeon.exe
dungeon.exe "go north" "go north" "take" "go south" "go east" "attack" "go north" "open" "look"
```

A single run exercises a native **state machine** (the treasure gate,
`Gate @ GateState::Locked` → `Unlocked`), **contracts**
(`requires self.room == 3` on `attack`), `Map`/`List` builtins, the
`Stack`/`Set` seed collections (the action history is a `Stack[String]`, visited
rooms a `Set[Int]`), **string parsing** (`trim` / `to_lower` / `split`), seeded
**randomness** (combat), and **file IO** (the run summary is written and read
back). The transcript ends `gold=100 hp=26 rooms=5 steps=9`.

Two language rules worth knowing when writing similar programs:

- command dispatch is a `match` on the verb string,
- struct literals must be single-line (statements are newline-terminated);
  nested literals are fine as long as the whole literal stays on one line.


# roadmap

# Language status

Aegis is a working compiler today. This page summarizes what the language and
standard library support, and what is still on the way.

## Language

- **Core values** - `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `Str`/`String`, and `Empty`, with
  stack-by-default memory and inferred automatic reference counting (ARC) for
  values that escape the current frame.
- **Control flow** - `if`/`else if`, `while`, the single `loop` form (bare,
  range, list, string, map), and `match` with guards, range patterns, `|`
  alternatives, and nested enum patterns.
- **Errors as values** - `Result[T, E]` / `Option[T]` with `ok`/`err`/`some`/
  `none` and `?` propagation.
- **Design by contract** - `requires` / `ensures` / `old(...)`, checked at
  runtime.
- **State machines and events** - `state`/`transition`, actor-style `emit`/`on`,
  `spawn`/`send`, and timers (`emit ... after`).
- **Abstraction** - `struct`/`impl`, traits (static and dynamic dispatch), user
  generics with bounds, and closures with the higher-order list methods
  (`map`/`filter`/`fold`/`sort`).
- **Modules** - multi-file compilation, `pub` visibility, and archive linking.
- **Enums** - user-defined sum types with payloads and exhaustive `match`.
- **Sized numeric widths** - `i8`..`u64` and `f32`, with explicit conversions.
- **Interop** - `extern "C"` (opaque handles, out params, C-string marshaling,
  function-pointer callbacks, and C-layout structs) and `export fn` for hosting
  Aegis code inside a C program.

## Standard library

- Math and transcendental functions, string operations, and `List`/`Map`
  builtins.
- In-Aegis collections: `Stack`, `Set`, `Queue`, and `Deque`.
- JSON parse/serialize, CSV encode/decode, and fixed-width tables.
- File IO and stdin; time and a seeded PRNG; `hash(x)`.
- Blocking TCP networking and a minimal HTTP/1.1 server.

## Tooling

- The `aegis` CLI: compile, format, and register the MCP server with your agent
  host.
- `aegis-mcp` serves the language corpus and build tools to agents over MCP;
  `aegis-daemon` / `aegis-ws` expose the streaming protocol.
- Installers and packaging for Windows (x64) and Linux (x86_64), including
  Scoop.

## On the way

- Cross-compilation between the supported targets.
- More standard-library depth: JSON pretty-printing and richer string and
  formatting helpers.
